bull_bear.body: Capex prioritized for growth (INR100cr FY26); no dividend or buyback mentioned; no debt used; focus on internal funding and organic expansion
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 4-wheeler revenue conversion timeline risk; supply chain disruption for imported LED chips (mitigated by multi-sourcing); delay in ambient/adaptive lighting adoption by OEMs; macro slowdown in auto demand
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, bullish on 2-wheeler growth, strategically patient on 4-wheeler entry; emphasis on in-house R&D, localization, and innovation; avoids overpromising on guidance but signals clear momentum
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Fiem is the sole supplier of animation lighting on TVS Norton — a global first in 2-wheelers — creating a defensible tech moat; the INR2.5cr provision reversal is a one-time accounting benefit, not operational; 4-wheeler RFQs include Mercedes, indicating premium OEM validation
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Effectively debt-free: long term loans (Rs. in mn) were 508 in FY21 and 205 in FY22, then 0 in each of FY23, FY24, FY25 and FY26; the balance sheet shows nil non-current and nil current borrowings at 31.03.24, 31.03.25 and 31.03.26.
- Dividend per share (Rs., marked restated on post-bonus share capital basis) has been raised every year: FY21 8, FY22 10, FY23 15, FY24 20, FY25 30, FY26 40.
- Consolidated cash and cash equivalents were 2,060 mn at 31.03.24, 2,983 mn at 31.03.25 and 2,794 mn at 31.03.26; total equity rose from 8,869 mn to 12,150 mn over the same three balance-sheet dates.
- Returns improved through the period — the deck's chart shows ROCE 11.66% / 19.62% / 25.08% / 24.96% / 26.22% / 28.02% and ROE 8.55% / 15.60% / 19.85% / 20.16% / 21.25% / 22.62% for FY21 through FY26.
- Working capital days lengthened from 9 in FY21 to 22-23 mid-period and 47 in FY26, while book value per share (Rs.) rose 218 / 246 / 289 / 366 / 393 / 460 across FY21-FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Deep, long-standing OEM relationships across leading 2W and 4W manufacturers (Yamaha, Suzuki, TVS, Honda, Royal Enfield, Hero, Mahindra & Mahindra, Daimler India, Kubota, Hyundai) evidenced by multiple annual cost/quality/delivery awards
- In-house R&D and validation infrastructure - NABL-accredited photometric laboratory, EMI/EMC testing lab, environmental/vibration/salt-spray chambers - reducing dependence on external testing and accelerating product development
- Backward-integrated manufacturing across moulding (injection/2K/3K moulding up to 1300T), electronics (SMT, robotic soldering) and tooling
- Technology partnerships/technical assistance agreements with Japanese majors - Aisan Industry Co., Ltd. and Toyodenso Co., Ltd. / Toyota Tsusho Corp.
- Global design/R&D footprint through wholly-owned subsidiaries in Japan and Italy and a Hong Kong JV, supporting international OEM and premium European car programs
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentrated OEM customer dependency — The Company supplies Rear View Mirrors to almost all of its OEM customers (predominantly two-wheeler) and is the sole supplier for several valued OEM customers' Rear View Mirror requirements - making performance sensitive to those OEMs' own programme volumes and sourcing decisions.
- Rapidly evolving industry/business environment — MD&A explicitly flags the automotive industry's rapidly evolving environment - changing customer preferences, technological advancements, geopolitical developments, supply chain disruptions, regulatory changes and macroeconomic uncertainties - as an ongoing risk requiring organisational resilience and agility.
- Cybersecurity risk — The Company's Enterprise Risk Management framework explicitly names cybersecurity risk arising from increasing digitalisation of business processes as a monitored risk category.
- Natural calamities and physical-asset risk (fire, theft, accidents) — ERM framework explicitly covers natural calamities that may disrupt manufacturing operations, and risks to the safety/security of employees, assets and infrastructure including fire, theft, accidents and other unforeseen events, addressed via preventive measures, protocols and periodic reviews.
- Foreign currency exchange rate risk — The Board-approved Risk Management Policy explicitly names foreign currency exchange rate risk as one of the risk categories covered by the Company's enterprise risk management framework.
- Market risk — The Risk Management Policy names market risk as one of the categories the framework is designed to identify, mitigate and monitor, alongside cyber, forex and natural-calamity risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: 2-wheeler: 97% of revenue; led penetration: 63.9% of lighting sales; key customers: TVS, Royal Enfield (6% rev), Yamaha, Hero, HMSI (25% rev); 4-wheeler: 3% of revenue; new awards: Mahindra HMSL, RR, fog, side repeater; RFQs active with Force Motors, Mercedes; no headlamp/taillamp awards yet but committed to entering all lamp types
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Deck describes FIEM as one of the leading manufacturers of Automotive Lighting & Signalling Equipment's and Rear View Mirrors in India, and among the first companies in India introducing LED lights in two wheelers; founded 1989 by Mr. J.K. Jain as Rahul Auto Private Limited and listed on BSE and NSE in 2006.
- Its major business comes from the two-wheeler segment — the FY26 automotive segment split is 2 Wheeler 97.15% / 4 Wheeler 2.85%.
- Strong client base of more than 50 OEMs, supplying prestigious customers since their inception: 2W — TVS, Honda, Yamaha, Suzuki, Royal Enfield, Harley Davidson, Hero Motocorp, Piaggio; 4W — Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, Force Motors, Ashok Leyland, Hyundai.
- Customer concentration is high and rising at the top: FY26 automotive segment contribution was TVS Motor Company 32.71%, Honda Two Wheeler Group 24.78%, India Yamaha 14.15%, Suzuki Motorcycle 9.25%, Royal Enfield 5.79%, Replacement Market 4.98%, Other Customers 8.34% (FY25: 27.84%, 27.80%, 14.90%, 9.25%, 4.60%, 5.67%, 9.94%).
- Exports go to Honda Japan, Harley Davidson (USA & Thailand) and Kubota Japan (tractors and farm equipment), besides OEMs in Austria, UK, Germany, Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam — though exports were only 1.85% of FY26 automotive segment revenue.

- [Leadership transition] With effect from June 01, 2026, founder Mr. J.K. Jain was re-designated Executive Chairman (from Chairman & Managing Director), Mr. Rahul Jain was elevated to Managing Director, and Ms. Aanchal Jain was re-designated Joint Managing Director; Mr. Rajesh Sharma continues as Joint Managing Director and Mr. Kashi Ram Yadav as Whole-time Director.
- [Bonus issue] FY22 and FY23 EPS figures in both the consolidated and standalone income statements, and several per-share charts, are footnoted RESTATED ON POST-BONUS SHARE CAPITAL BASIS.

- [Fuel pump JV] In 2018 FIEM entered a Joint Venture with Aisan Industry Co. Ltd., Japan and Toyota Tsusho India Pvt. Ltd. for manufacture of Fuel Pump Module for the Indian market.
- [Regulatory approvals] The Integrated Passenger Information System with LED Display (IPIS) holds approval from the Ministry of Railways - Research Design and Standard Organization (RDSO) for train indication, coach guidance and PC-based announcement, and the Association of State Road Transport Undertakings inspected the LED based Destination system and found it satisfactory.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Vision to be a dominant player in automotive lighting by developing innovative technologies, and to build a trusted, safe, self-reliant and sustainable global organisation.
- Continue investing ahead of the curve - strengthening technological capabilities, expanding manufacturing infrastructure and developing innovative products to create lasting customer value.
- Growth strategy to be supported by strong internal accruals, prudent capital allocation and a healthy balance sheet, pursuing growth with financial discipline and long-term sustainability.
- Grow the four-wheeler business as an important pillar of long-term growth strategy, building on the newly commenced supply relationship with Mahindra & Mahindra and a growing PV customer base.
- Build in-house electronics design, validation and testing capability (EMI/EMC lab) to strengthen engineering depth, speed up product development and reduce dependence on external testing facilities.
- Pursue a green-energy/sustainability journey (rooftop solar and open-access renewable power across plants) in support of a long-term carbon-neutral objective.
- Mission to be market leader across products through global competitiveness, with a customer-focused approach to safety, quality, cost and on-time delivery.
- Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted 30 June 2021 pursuant to SEBI Listing Regulation 43A, applicable as the Company is among the top 1000 listed entities by market capitalisation) guides recommendation/declaration of interim and final dividends based on financial parameters and internal/external factors, and how retained earnings are utilised. The Company states it has been consistently declaring higher dividends every year since listing. Broader growth strategy is stated to be supported by strong internal accruals, prudent capital allocation and a healthy balance sheet, pursuing growth with financial discipline and long-term sustainability.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26 the Company commissioned and inaugurated a new state-of-the-art EMI/EMC Testing Laboratory at its R&D-Electronics, Innovation Centre & Corporate Office in Gurugram, to enable in-house EMI/EMC validation of automotive lighting products for two-wheelers and four-wheelers, strengthen backward integration in engineering/validation infrastructure and reduce dependence on external testing facilities. In parallel, the Company began a green-energy rollout - rooftop solar and open-access renewable power - starting at its Hosur plant (~65% of energy needs via open-access solar, with a further ~20% being added via wind energy), with similar initiatives being progressively extended to other manufacturing locations. Separately, reinstatement is under way at the fire-damaged Tapukara Unit-VIII (fire of 23 August 2025): undamaged Ground Floor/Basement production resumed on 29 August 2025, while as an interim measure production set-up for Bank Angle Sensor (BAS) and 4-Wheeler (especially Mahindra & Mahindra) parts was reinstated at the Rai Plant (Unit-VII) and restarted in September 2025; full building/machinery reinstatement at Tapukara continues. The Rai Plant's own re-instatement (from the June 2023 fire) was completed during the year, with the insurance claim assessment in its final stages.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Two-wheeler segment expected to remain central to India's mobility landscape given its affordability, utility and deep relevance across urban, semi-urban and rural markets.
- Premiumisation, connected features, safety regulations and electric mobility are steadily reshaping customer expectations and product architecture across vehicle categories.
- For automotive lighting specifically, the transition from conventional lighting to LED, projector lamps, DRLs, ambient lighting, adaptive and intelligent lighting systems is increasing the value content of lighting per vehicle.
- Rising safety awareness, stricter regulatory expectations, premiumisation of two-wheelers/passenger vehicles and increasing OEM design differentiation are expected to support demand for advanced lighting products.
- Companies with strong design capabilities, engineering depth, cost competitiveness and close OEM relationships are expected to remain better positioned in this evolving environment.
- Auto component industry expected to be a key beneficiary of OEM localisation, supply-chain resilience, cost optimisation and technology partnerships, across both domestic and export markets.
- Electrification remains one of the most important long-term industry themes, with electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler segments seen as early beneficiaries of policy support and expanding product availability.
- Growing vehicle complexity - higher electronic content, LED lighting systems, sensors, controllers, wiring and thermal management - expected to create new avenues for value-added component manufacturing.
- Structural domestic demand drivers cited: low vehicle penetration versus developed markets, rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, improved financing availability and higher replacement demand.
- Four-wheeler business described as supported by 'a growing customer base and a healthy order pipeline', with management confident of strengthening its position in this high-value segment.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Fiem delivered record Q2FY26 revenue and PAT driven by strong 2-wheeler demand and higher-margin LED product mix, while making strategic inroads into 4-wheeler lighting with new Mahindra awards and advanced tech like animation lighting — the shift from 3% to >10% 4-wheeler revenue share over the next 12–18 months is the key value driver.

open.item: Gogoro facing significant international headwinds; India strategy unclear and project on pause; investment under INR10 crores and reimbursable; tech transfer expected in next couple of quarters but may be delayed.
State-of-the-art EMC/EMI electronic validation lab (first of its kind in Indian auto lighting) under installation, to be commissioned in the next quarter.
Capex of INR38 cr in H1; expect another INR50-60 crores in H2, totaling ~INR100 crores for FY26, with momentum to continue in line with growth.
Hero Glamour X 125 (projector headlamp) and Xtreme (LED winker) in production; more models under development, with next half expected even better for Hero.
Clearer four-wheeler business planning / revenue picture to be shared by end of this financial year, plus a direction on a dedicated plant.
Management expects H2 FY26 to be better and the full year could be the highest-ever two-wheeler production year, surpassing the FY19-20 peak.
Company to add another 10 SMT lines over the next year, from the current 10 lines.
Company reiterates 15-20% revenue growth guidance for FY27 and belief it will outperform the industry; no specific numeric guidance beyond that.
Margin reached ~14% on product mix and operating leverage; management hoping to work around the 14% mark going forward (vs prior 13-14% guidance) and views it as sustainable.
No stock split or bonus under discussion, having just completed a bonus in 2024.
Dutch chipmaker Nexperia global issues flagged; Fiem uses multi-source discrete electronic components so no production hold-up expected in coming months.
Ambient lighting proof-of-concept demonstrated and appreciated by a customer; company expects to be on the ambient light supplier panel very soon.
Royal Enfield is ~6% of sales with >90% share on Classic lamps; management expects an uptick above 6% going forward on volumes and new models.
Four-wheeler RFQ value remains ~INR700 crores (some converted, new ones from Force Motors); RFQs also in progress with Mercedes; more than 100 projects overall worth ~INR1,000-1,200 crores.
Steep US tariffs (up to 50%) create sector headwinds but Fiem is unaffected as direct US business is marginal and on FOB terms with tariffs borne by customers.
Replacement/aftermarket business declining as lamps shift from conventional to LED (longer life); may fluctuate quarter-on-quarter, partly offset by non-direct-customer models.
Management clarified the June promoter stake sale was small, first in decades, for personal use, with no plan for further stake sale.
Management acknowledged a shareholder buyback suggestion, saying it is discussed at Board level but priority is capital for future growth over 3-5 years.
Management flagged Europe market slowdown affecting export business but views it as seasonal, not a consolidated revenue risk.
Seven projects under development to be launched in 2024, 2025 and over the next three years, ~90% new models, split domestic and export.

verdicts.item: Two Hero models (incl. X440 Harley-Davidson) in production; two more to launch in next two quarters, with additional projects for FY25.
verdicts.note: 'There are two models which from Hero is being launched. It is being already converted into a mass production and a sales' (Glamour X 125, Xtreme winker).

verdicts.item: Capex guidance INR125-150 crores for FY25 (INR108 cr spent in 9M, ~INR25 cr in Q4) and INR75-100 crores additional next year, excluding any new greenfield four-wheeler plant.
verdicts.note: 'our capex for the current year should be INR100 crores' (H1 INR37.81 cr, +INR50-60 cr H2), in line with the earlier guidance; no greenfield 4W plant.

wtt.summary: 68% guidance hit (14 chains); 5/8 projects on-time; 15% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Highly confident on record numbers and margin sustainability at ~14%; owned Yamaha's softer quarter and PV revenue still being insignificant; deferred four-wheeler revenue and plant decisions to year-end as usual.
